reasoning: The narration makes a compelling concrete comparison between two specific functions (3n² + 5n + 2 vs 2n log n + 100) but the tool cannot show this comparison visually. Students are left hearing about domination without seeing it happen. This violates the core principle of visual-verbal alignment - the tool must support the narrative claim with direct visual evidence.

strengths: Uses concrete, specific functions instead of abstract examples
Builds intuition about large input behavior
Appropriate level of technical detail for undergraduates
weaknesses: References visual evidence ('that n² term will absolutely dominate') that the tool cannot provide
Doesn't explain the c and n₀ symbols mentioned in formal definition
Claims 'every single time' without showing the mathematical proof

requirements.description: Function comparison mode that plots both 3n² + 5n + 2 and 2n log n + 100 on the same axes with different colors
requirements.reason: Students need to see the specific functions being compared, not abstract curves

requirements.description: Crossover point highlighter that shows where n log n stops winning and n² takes over permanently
requirements.reason: Makes the 'domination' concept visually concrete rather than just asserted

requirements.description: Animated slider that grows n from small values to large (1 to 10,000) showing the gap between functions increase
requirements.reason: Dynamic visualization of how asymptotic behavior emerges as n grows

requirements.description: Numerical table showing concrete millisecond values at key n values (10, 100, 1000, 10000)
requirements.reason: Provides concrete numbers that make the abstract concept tangible
